name: J03 - real approvals for read, edit and shell
about: J03 - real read / edit / shell approvals, and what each one actually did.
PURPOSE. The product gates these three tools on a real permission. Three
approvals are driven, one per tool, against production authority.
PRECONDITION. The retained client must NOT be launched with --auto or
--dangerously-skip-permissions; in auto mode it answers every request
without drawing a prompt, and the run FAILS at the visible-ask step.
AN APPROVAL IS NOT AN EXECUTION. Neither the ask disappearing nor any value
the model could compute establishes that a tool RAN. Two independent things
are required after every allow, and a generic substring is neither:
1. THE NAMED CALL SETTLES, asserted as ONE string so the action and its
terminal cannot be satisfied by two different rows. Native renders
`tool <name> <status>`, so `tool shell completed` binds both. Retained
uses its own verbs, which change with status and are therefore just as
bound: Ran (index.tsx:2867, Running while in flight), Read (:2976,
Reading while in flight) and Edited (:3177).
2. THE BYTES ON DISK, for shell and edit, read outside the client entirely.
THE EFFECT IS BRACKETED. Before the shell prompt the file must be MISSING -
the strict claim that nothing was written, not merely that it lacks a
marker - so a leftover from an earlier run cannot be mistaken for this
run's work. It is asserted missing again WHILE the ask is outstanding, then
present after the allow. The edit step brackets the NEW marker the same way.
READ HAS NO ON-DISK EFFECT and is not given a fake one. Natively its evidence
is its own settled row, `tool read completed`, which names the action and its
terminal in one string.
THE RETAINED READ IS ASSERTED ON ITS GROUPED ROW, and getting here took two
wrong answers worth recording.
First I waited for `Read`, which timed out while the call had in fact
COMPLETED - the durable record shows `call_e4ihE3heXMcqzMwfVOv49cnU`
completed with a 13-byte output whose digest matches the native read exactly.
`Read` appears only in the PERMISSION PREVIEW and vanishes when the ask is
answered.
Then I concluded the settled state shows only the file's content. Wrong
again: it renders a GROUPED exploration row, `Explored - 1 read`
(index.tsx:1470), and `Explored` versus `Exploring` is exactly a completion
discriminator. I had searched for capital `Read` and missed a row that says
`read`.
IT IS ONE STRING, `Explored — 1 read`, so completion, tool and count are
bound adjacently rather than able to match three different rows.
AN EARLIER REVISION SPLIT IT INTO TWO ASCII SUBSTRINGS on the belief that the
capture mangled the em dash. That belief was FALSE and the corruption was in
my own analysis script: it read the screen JSON with `open()`, which on this
machine defaults to cp1252, so correct UTF-8 arrived as three characters. The
raw pty transcript holds the clean bytes, the screen JSON holds them, and the
harness decodes its responses with an explicit `.decode("utf-8")`. Nothing
in the product or the capture path corrupts anything.
product told the user.
project from the launch directory it is handed; native's is the service
root, a git boundary of its own. Both are passed explicitly and RECORDED in
the receipt as effect_root, and a path escaping its own root is refused.
THE COMMAND IS SPELLED OUT, and that is a correction from an actual run, not
caution. Asked to 'create a file whose contents are ALPHAMARKER', the model
reached for `printf`, which the shell tool ran through cmd.exe on Windows:
shell exited with exit code: 1; captured output: 'printf' is not recognized
as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.
The redirection had ALREADY created the file, so it sat at ZERO BYTES, and
the model then retried with a PowerShell one-liner - raising a SECOND ask this
scenario never answered. Naming the exact command removes that variance at its
cause. It is not an approval loop and does not compensate for a product
defect: the tool ran, failed, and recorded `failed / effect-failed` with the
captured output.
AND NOTE WHAT THAT ZERO-BYTE FILE MEANS: a failed command CAN leave a
filesystem side effect. `effect-failed` is not proof that nothing was
written, and this scenario does not treat it as such. It is why the file is
asserted MISSING before the prompt rather than merely lacking its marker -
a previous failed attempt leaves a real file behind.
LIMITATION. Whether the model reaches for the named tool at all is still model
behaviour. A model that does not is a bounded timeout at the ask or at the
settled row - a reported run failure, never an acceptance.
